_comment: Pocky's evaluation set (npm run agent:eval). Fictional content only. Records come from agent-fixture.json; every figure in a mustContain is recomputed from it by test/agentEval.test.ts. Reply needles are case-insensitive and compare numbers by value (thousands separators and trailing decimal zeros ignored; a numeric needle must match a whole number). mustNotMatch patterns use flags 'mi'.

cases.message: I have 2,000 in chequing today. Rent of 1,100 is due Nov 1, a tuition top-up of 1,500 on Nov 5, and I get paid 1,800 on Nov 10. What's the lowest my balance will get before the end of November?
cases.note: Lowest end-of-day balance is -600.00 on 2026-11-05.

cases.message: If co-op pays $2,400 a biweekly from September, can I save $5,000 by December based on my overall spending habit?
cases.note: Mirrors a production failure (agent_limit_exceeded): a biweekly pay schedule plus a spending baseline. Before the fix DeepSeek reasoned by default (thinking blocks counted against the output budgets) and biweekly pay could only be modelled as weekly. The turn must finish inside the limits; it may project with a two_weeks repeat or ask for cash on hand, but must not promise the goal is reachable.

cases.message: My first co-op paycheque of $1,250 lands on Friday, October 16, 2026, and then every two weeks after that. How many paydays do I get before December 31, 2026, and how much is that in total?
cases.note: Six paydays (Oct 16, Oct 30, Nov 13, Nov 27, Dec 11, Dec 25), 7,500.00 in total. Pocky once said 8 payments for a biweekly schedule; the count must come from calculate_scenario's event_counts. An income-only question, so no baseline is needed.

cases.message: Analyze my spending habits.
cases.note: Habits need a long enough window: a 3-month baseline mixes a study term with a work term. Pocky must average 12 months or compare whole terms.

cases.message: My co-op pays 1,980 every two weeks; the work term runs from September to the end of December. Estimate whether my savings can get to around 4,200 by the end of December, and analyze my past spending habits.
cases.note: Mirrors a production reply (2026-10-15) with different figures: it read only a 3-month baseline and offered a projection starting September 1. Habits need 12 months or a term comparison; any projection starts today (start omitted or not in the past); without cash on hand it must ask rather than call the goal reachable.

cases.message: I have 2,000 in savings today. My co-op pays 1,700 every two weeks starting October 23 until the end of December. Can my savings be around 5,000 by the end of December? Also analyze my spending habits.
cases.note: Mirrors a QA reply (2026-10-15, different figures) that invented rent 1,240 + 600 living a month and called the goal comfortably within reach. No expenses are stated, so they must come from spending_baseline (12 months: 2,086.77 a month). Charged monthly from today that ends December near 4,240, short of 5,000; the invented 1,840 a month ends near 4,980, which reads as reached. Asking for expenses instead of projecting also passes. Adding the baseline income on top of the stated pay double-counts it and ends near 8,653, so the reply must not call 5,000 reachable either.
